If you're asking why vertex sets are useful as opposed to them always being .univ, you can go through the discussions linked here. Basically we like to add/remove vertices to graphs, and since the vertex type is a parameter of SimpleGraph rather than a field this is very hard to do without DTT issues.

Could we somehow accelerate the merging of #38476? It has been sitting in the review queue for a while, especially when including its predecessor #33466. Merging it and then adding vertex sets to SimpleGraph would unblock a lot of algorithms theory related to graphs including graph minors.

Cc : @Basil Rohner

Ah, found the right thread: #graph theory > Set in definition of Graph @ 💬

There seems to be some agreement yes. The idea was to add them to docs#Digraph first since it has thin API. Quite a few order theory design issues came up. Those are the PRs I mentioned above. docs#SimpleGraph has a lot of material built on top of it. So porting it will be harder.

Shreyas Srinivas said:

docs#SimpleGraph has a lot of material built on top of it. So porting it will be harder.

I think GraphLike is the right move for this, since it'll allow us to port iteratively, by generalizing theorems/defs one-by-one from SimpleGraph to GraphLike.
Alternatively we could add a vertex set and then also a class IsUnivSimpleGraph that says G.verts = .univ that every theorem will assume, and then we'll remove it one-by-one. But GraphLike is a win-win here IMO.
If you use GraphLike, would SimpleGraph get vertex sets as well? I was under the impression that you would still have to add vertex sets explicitly to make SimpleGraph an instance of GraphLike.

I haven't looked into the details of the current state of GraphLike, but I imagine we could do something like

instance {V : Type*} : GraphLike V Dart (Sym2 V) (SimpleGraph V) where
  verts G := Set.univ
  Adj G := G.Adj
  ...

so we can avoid adding a verts field to SimpleGraph until we finish migration
Ooh, exactly like that, Jun Kwon opened #39054 2 minutes ago, nice :)

Okay but we also want to change SimpleGraph to have proper vertex sets and this just seems to keep SimpleGraph as it is. Concretely, it would be nice to have vertex sets asap, even before the Graph API based migration happens. It unblocks a bunch of graph algorithmic reasoning downstream. Waiting several months for this migration process seems to block downstream work for too long.

Shreyas Srinivas said:

it would be nice to have vertex sets asap

Sure but there's reality. A huge huge refactor takes time, no matter how bad we want it. And especially one we want to be well thought out.
You're welcome to try and one-shot it of course, but I'm very much against against such an attempt.
Could those algorithms use GraphLike directly? If so, they could work as soon as the relavant parts are generalized.

btw for comparison, Loogle reports 57 decls about Digraph, and 3265 decls about SimpleGraph (≈ 57²).
So if your plan is to repeat the Digraph PR but for SimpleGraphs, I think you're looking at multiple months or even years of work and review time (unless LLMs will somehow become more viable for Mathlib).
I'm not sure if this is really linear, but the Digraph PR started on January and isn't merged yet, so 4 months * 57 ≈ 19 years.
Which is why I suggested a community effort to collab and get this over the line much quicker, and also IMO it'll be much more fun.
Although there's a chance only the Lattice instances are what's taking so long, and that refactoring theorems is trivial and so it's absolutely not linear and will be quick, but idk. Maybe the IsUnivSimpleGraph idea could work and get vertex sets in a single PR.

For what its worth, I am very much committed in getting GraphLike series of PRs merged ASAP. In Matroid repo, I have cycle matroid of a graph, Menger's theorem for finite graph, existence of an edge that can be contracted keeping 3-connectivity assuming more than 4 vertices, all blocked by GraphLike.
If there is anything I am doing that is slowing the process down, that is me being ignorant so please let me know.
Sounds good to me. Is there a roadmap we can follow to contribute byte-sized PRs?

Since someone suggested that minors would require working with Graph instead of SimpleGraph -- not so! I have (in a private repo, that I hope to be able to announce soon) some work on this notion of minor:

/-- A minor model of a graph `H` in a graph `G` consists of an assignment of each vertex
of `H` to a nonempty connected subset of vertices of `G` (called a "branch set"),
such that the branch sets are pairwise disjoint, and for each edge `{u, v}` in `H`,
there exists an edge in `G` between the branch sets of `u` and `v`. -/
structure MinorModel (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The branch set assignment: each vertex of H maps to a set of vertices of G. -/
  branchSet : W → Set V
  /-- Each branch set is nonempty. -/
  branchSet_nonempty : ∀ w : W, (branchSet w).Nonempty
  /-- The induced subgraph on each branch set is connected. -/
  branchSet_connected : ∀ w : W, (G.induce (branchSet w)).Connected
  /-- Branch sets for distinct vertices are disjoint. -/
  branchSet_disjoint : ∀ u v : W, u ≠ v → Disjoint (branchSet u) (branchSet v)
  /-- For each edge of H, there is an edge in G between the corresponding branch sets. -/
  branchSet_adj : ∀ u v : W, H.Adj u v →
    ∃ x ∈ branchSet u, ∃ y ∈ branchSet v, G.Adj x y

and it seems to have worked out quite well for me so far. I have facts such as that being a minor is transitive and that treewidth is monotonic in minors.

If you're thinking of a graph minor in terms of 'allowed operations' of deletion/contraction, I strongly advise against that, because this does not produce the correct notion of minor for infinite graphs. Minors are really a type of morphism (and the 'minor' relationship does carry data!)
Nitpick: I think branchSet_connected implies branchSet_nonempty

Although I really like this sentence:

Alex Meiburg said:

Minors are really a type of morphism

and I think this approach isn't blocked by vertex sets and sounds promising! I'd love to see a f : H →gm G where gm is "graph minor". #36210 does look similar but it hides the mapping behind an ∃.

Yes, I guess it's cleanest for f : G →c H for saying that H is a contraction of G: this has a FunLike instance (and is closed under composition, etc.). That's really a nice relationship then. Could call it a contraction, or a spanning minor. That's the

def IsContraction (G : SimpleGraph V) (G' : SimpleGraph V') : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : V' → V, Surjective φ ∧ Adapted G' φ ∧ G = G'.map φ

in #36210. I guess minors are bit uglier, to handle the deleted vertices. I mean, the relationship is fine to state, but the G →gm H doesn't give you a G → H function. You can get a PFun out, or a G → Option H, where the none would represent vertex deletion. But if you're okay with this funny behavior of the FunLike, then yeah, you could define this structure and that would work fine.

I think this is very similar to, but just kind of backwards from, the structure MinorData in Yael's example or in my structure MinorModel. There you have the branchSet : W → Set V, with the guarantee that the images are disjoint sets; this is just asking for the unique partial inverse of that function.

I proposed a defintion like that in this thread. Peter Nelson pointed out that we prefer set theoretic definitions

https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/116395-maths/topic/Graph.20Minors/near/579990939
I called it a subjective homomorphism from a graph to the minor graph.
Ah, I'd missed that. Yeah. But then you still need to account for deletion somehow. Surely the zero-vertex graph is a minor of every graph, but there are no homomorphisms to it.
the contracting homomorphism only captures edge contractions. A graph minor would be a subgraph of a contracted graph
But then they aren't 'obviously' transitive, which is unfortunate. The data structure for a minor model should, on some level, naturally compose.
(I agree that a contraction homomorphism belongs in Mathlib and is valuable in its own right)
Also @Marcin Pilipczuk you might be interested in this thread. Especially the PR.

A quick update on current progress: The first phase of theorems are now complete on my own branch tree_decomp_develop, and I will organize the code into several PRs in the coming days.

Currently I have proved:

  • treewidth_top: The treewidth of a complete graph with $n$ vertices is $n-1$.
  • adhesion_imp_separator: The adhesion set of some edge in the tree decomposition is a graph separator (with basic definitions for graph separators)
  • isAcyclic_iff_treewidth: A graph is acyclic iff its treewidth <= 1.

Note that adding IsAcyclic/IsTree to Subgraphs probably won't get merged, perhaps you could inline their definition where you use them?
and IsSeparator should probably be defined using docs#SimpleGraph.deleteEdges to match docs#SimpleGraph.IsEdgeReachable

The Subgraph.IsAcyclic predicate ended up being unused, I've just removed them.

For IsSeparator, what I need here is vertex separators (the same type used for Menger's theorem), which are different from edge separators (used for min cut/max flow), so I don't think IsEdgeReachable is applicable here. I would prefer adopting @Jun Kwon's SetCut design eventually, but my current code is a working simplified version.

I didn't suggest you use IsEdgeReachable, I suggested you use deleteEdges
